items.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You’re talking about Saddam Hussein? [INTERVIEWEE] Saddam. There was all of this kind of same thing in the changing over from the ’60s into the ’70s.

ctx.x: Saddam. There was all of this kind of same thing in the changing over from the ’60s into the ’70s. The feeling about, you can do something, to go back to America, and maybe you can do something about what’s going on. Can you wake people up? What’s Going On? was a beautiful – it is the most beautiful piece I heard at the time. It remains that, because it talks about what is happening. Listen to the Silence talks about what was happening then. So I like to have, behind the music, a reason for the music. That’s it.

What was happening with the Lydian Concept at this point? Were you – it’s been a work in progress. It was being developed over time, and now you’re teaching it. Were you teaching every day? Three days a week? What kind of schedule do you recall?
